First let me say that Chantix DOES work.  If you want to quit and you take the medicine as prescribed, it will be a significant factor in helping you quit.  

I quit using Chantix at the 2 month mark, earlier than recommended, because I could not deal with the cumulative side effects.  At the time I quit taking it, I was totally smoke-free for 6 weeks. I am still smoke free.  

The side effects I experienced included:  (1) vivid dreams (but not what i would consider nightmares) that did impact my quality of sleep; (2) significant gas, so I had to get creative with excusing myself; (3) moodiness, ranging from lack of interest (mild depression?) to outright intolerance (quick to anger; (4) constipation, which is easy to fix but contributed to my moodiness; (5) weight gain, even when carefully monitoring what goes in my mouth and 50 mins of daily exercise, which also contributed to my moodiness, and (6) nausea, regardless of when I took it.  In the end, it was the nausea and mood swings, coupled with the fear that I was experiencing some level of depression, that caused me to stop taking Chantix.    

I experienced minimal withdrawal symptoms, I think, with the most significant being short intense but infrequent. This lasted for about 3-4 days.  My mood is much better, I can focus, but weight is still a problem for me, but I'm working on that too.  And since I do not have my Chantix crutch, my new mantra is "There is no such thing as "just one" (cigarette)."  I do not want to go through quitting again, and having to make a choice about which "aid" to use - I probably would not start with Chantix the next time.  Good luck!

I started taking Celexa 20mg (generic citalopram, its a lot cheaper) The first week of August this year. I was diagnosed with Major Depression and Generalized Anxiety Disorder. I take it once a day at night (with food to diminish any possible gastrointestinal side effects). I am feeling 100% better than I did just a few months ago. I could not be more satisfied with the outcome. Before, I could not sleep or focus on anything. I was nauseas and exhausted all of the time and I even felt so dizzy I couldnt drive or go to class. I am now falling asleep without the help of sleep-aids. I have energy again; I no longer sleep 8 hours and wake up feeling more exhausted than I did the night before. FOR ME this was the correct medication. NO MEDICATION IS CORRECT FOR EVERYONE. There are several negative reviews from individuals; take them with a grain of salt. Yes, the first week can be miserable on a new anti-depressant (you have serotonin receptors all over your body, including your brain, blood vessels and stomach. While your body is adjusting to the new levels of serotonin, you will probably feel nauseas and have a headache). You have to be patient though! After a week I could feel a difference, and after a month I felt great. I feel like my old self again. The only downside I can find with the drug is that I cannot drink AT ALL on this drug. As with most SSRIs, alcohol renders the medication ineffective because Alcohol occupies the same receptors in your body. Massive panic attacks came for an entire week after drinking moderately. I would happily give up alcohol for the rest of my life to NEVER feel the depression and anxiety ever again though. There are also sexual side effects, but for me they have been positive. I can now maintain an erection and have a healthy sex life. I also have no problem with having orgasms. Do not rule out any drug because of the reviews on here. Eventually, you WILL find the right drug for you :). HANG IN THERE!!

The NuvaRing looks great on the surface: easy, impossible to forget, effective.  And, generally, this proved to be true in the eight months I used it.  However, there's something doctors don't tell you: the NuvaRing can cause chronic yeast infections.  

Now, I'm not entirely sure why this is, as I've gotten differing explanations from different doctors (so reassuring, right?): one doctor said it's because the vagina sees the NuvaRing as a foreign body and "attacks" it (this makes little sense to me--why would the YEAST be attacking?); another said that the yeast coats and clings to the surface of the NuvaRing, causing an overgrowth and, then, a yeast infection.  Research I've done since this problem began has offered me more illuminating facts about birth control (ALL birth controls): 1) birth control can change the pH of the vagina (the good bacteria that keep the yeast at bay only thrive at a certain pH and a change disrupts their abilities, thus causing yeast growth) and 2) birth control raises blood sugar (sugar feeds the yeast--higher blood sugar = more chance of yeast overpopulation).

Before I went on the NuvaRing, I had perfect vaginal health.  I had not had a yeast infection in years and very rarely had any kind of vaginal itching or discomfort.  Since starting the NuvaRing in January of this year, I have had one yeast infection after another, first once a month and then (NOW) pretty much constantly.  I have been on yeast infection medication (a mix of Diflucan and Monistat 3-day) for an entire month, have been taking probiotics, grapefruit seed extract, and garlic tablets, have been eating a 99% anti-Candida diet, AND THE YEAST INFECTION IS STILL NOT GONE.

Now, maybe this is not a common thing.  Maybe my case is singular, my body somehow more prone to yeast infections (though my five year history pre-birth control would negate that), but I doubt it.  


Bottom line: I would seriously consider another option before starting the NuvaRing.

I've come to the conclusion that Mobic, when used correctly for specific types of joint pain, can be very helpful. When used  'shotgun-style' for all types of pain, it is not effective. Having dealt with Anxiety, Depression, PTSD, and OCD for the last 10 years -- Zoloft has helped me immensely.  In my experience it starts to alleviate symptoms w/in 1-2 weeks, but finding the correct dosage is critical; too high of a dose tended to promote mania for me.

First, I tried Paxil for 1 1/2 years but my experience with it at 10-40mg was that Paxil, although effective, made me feel “mentally numb."
 
A switch to Zoloft proved to better treat my symptoms without the “numbness.” But I was still symptomatic for 2 years while taking only 100mg.  After an increase to 150mg I felt much better, but had to watch out for manic episodes.  

Side effects: these are well documented.  Starting, stopping, increasing/decreasing brings on: "electric shock" sensations in arms and legs, waking up frequently at night, clenching one's jaw while sleeping, and disturbing lucid dreams.  At times I felt I was losing my mind, especially when I abruptly stopped taking the medication.  It has been my experience that these side effects abate w/in 2 weeks.

Also to note: for anxiety and mania, caffeine is the devil!!  Switching to decaf was essential to my progress.  Even just one cup o' joe would launch me into major anxiety and/or mania for days.  I can't stress enough how critical this was for me.

Sexual side effects: yeah, they’re a problem.  My gf told me I “needed to have a long talk with Mr. Wiener.”  We broke up.  It helps to have a girlfriend who is supportive, not selfish, about your progress.

In conclusion, including Zoloft as a part of my therapy has opened doors for me that have been shut for years.  After a stressful six-year military career, and having up and quit seven jobs since, failing in semester after semester of college, surviving a school shooting, and a tragic end to a 2-year relationship, I was suicidal every day.  Taking Zoloft helped me overcome my symptoms for Anxiety, Depression, PTSD, and OCD, and helped me get back living again.

My tolerance has not increased in the 3+ years I've been using this med, as compared to all the others. The dose is long acting, plus I don't need to take as much to relieve my pain. This medication takes a few days to get into your system properly, so don't be impatient and exceed your dose. As it cannot be refilled over the phone at your neighborhood pharmacy, if you run out before your next appt. you may experience some degree of opiate withdrawal. Rather than go 'cold turkey',  you can probably take a little less for a few days in order to build up a supply to help you thru til your next appt. Use common sense.

Methadone can be a helpful medication if taken properly. A proper dialogue between doctor and patient is necessary in order to find the proper dose and minimize complications. In addition, you, the patient, should do some research and make an informed choice as to what path you should take.

a lollipops handy to suck on after for any after taste. I started my second liter at 4pm. The prep worked pretty quickly, it hit me around 6pm, and the evacuation (for lack of a better word). Tip: keep alcohol-free wipes handy and "pat" dry instead of wiping with tp each time to keep from getting that sore, burny feeling. I was running somewhat clear by 10pm.

I came to this site today to review opinions between "Brand" and generic Adderrall and thought I should add my personal experience with this medication.

I was diagnosed with depression 14 years ago and was prescribed Paxil. After six months of little change in my condition, I was prescribed Prozac and Xanax. Over the next few years, my conditioned worsened. I was eventually prescribed Ambien for insomnia, which was a huge mistake.

I became addicted to Ambien, not for the sleep benefits but for the Utopian feeling it provided me. I would take it several times during the day, and quickly began running out of my prescriptions. This led to "Doc Shopping," and eventually I had three doctors writing me scripts every month.

Long story short: my marriage fell apart, I couldn't hold a job and I reached a point where I didn't care whether I lived or died.

Three years ago, I made an appt. with a young doctor at a university research facility. After describing my medical history and my current condition, he said he believed I suffered from adult ADD. He started me on 10 mg of Adderall daily.

Within two months, I was completely off my depression meds (Cymbalta and Tofrenil) and had no desire whatsoever for the Ambien. 

I have now been taking 30 mg daily for the past year, and am experiencing no addictive drug behavior whatsoever. I was also a daily drinker, and now only drink 1-2 glasses of wine on the weekends. I have held a steady, professional-level job for over three years now, and my marriage has been restored.

Through the grace of God, I was led to a doctor who literally saved my life. This amazing drug has helped make all the difference. If you have been diagnosed with depression and nothing seems to help, you may want to discuss this with your doctor.

I spoke to my doctor and we agreed that at 20mg I achieved results so I scaled back down.

None of them were unbearable for me (although the RLS and insomnia did make for some very long nights). The medication has worked for me.
